headline: JPMorgan's single AI model improved card fraud detection by up to 85.5%, its paper says
body: JPMorgan built a single AI model for fraud detection, payment authorization predictions and retries, trained on up to 400 billion tokens of card, ACH and wire transaction data. Compared with the bank's task-specific models, the researchers wrote that card fraud detection improved by up to 85.5%, measured by average precision. The paper includes no figures on fraud losses, false declines or cost savings.
note: The second version reads up to six months of prior transactions tied to the same party, and that history pushed the fraud detection gain to 85.5%. Every result is measured on JPMorgan's own card and treasury payments, and the paper does not test against a public benchmark.

figure.label: Card fraud detection gain, up to, over task-specific models

evidence.text: JPMorgan built a single AI model for fraud detection, payment authorization predictions and retries, trained on up to 400 billion tokens of card, ACH and wire transaction data.
The model improved card fraud detection by up to 85.5%, ACH fraud detection by 27.4% and payment retry predictions by 22.8% compared with the bank’s task-specific models.
The measure, average precision, tracks how well a model ranks rare fraud cases above legitimate payments, the researchers said.
Building a separate model for each one means teaching every model the same payment patterns again, the bank’s researchers wrote in a paper published Nov. 11.
The paper does not name those models, give their absolute scores or test LPM against a public benchmark.
It includes no figures on fraud losses, false declines or cost savings.
Every result is a gain over JPMorgan’s own single-task models, measured on the bank’s own card and treasury payments, the researchers said.
The second version reads up to six months of prior transactions tied to the same party.
That history pushed the fraud detection gain to 85.5%.
